description: SDLC-support products that help plan, implement, review, test, secure, modernize, or maintain software. General-purpose agent application platforms, frameworks, eval tools, and guardrails live in agents.json.

categories.description: Agents that can take tickets, prompts, issues, or tasks and independently modify repositories, run tests, and produce pull requests or deployable application changes.
Interactive coding agents embedded in IDEs, terminals, editors, or local developer environments.
Enterprise developer-platform agents that combine coding, repository intelligence, cloud context, DevSecOps workflows, governance, modernization, and organizational controls.
Agents focused on pull request review, bug finding, standards enforcement, test coverage, CI feedback, and code quality governance.

options.name: OpenAI Codex Agent
options.notes: Developer agent for cloud, CLI, IDE, and desktop workflows. Supports repository edits, debugging, PR suggestions, parallel long-running tasks, skills, Agent Plugins, MCP (2026-07-28 spec), and supervised terminal-local approvals. Codex CLI 0.146/0.147 (Jul 29-Aug 7, 2026) added session naming, thread pinning, and portable Agent Plugins; a Linux desktop app entered preview (Aug 11) with import of Claude Code and Cursor setups. GPT-5.4 retires from ChatGPT-authenticated Codex on Aug 31, 2026 in favor of GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna.

options.name: Claude Code
options.notes: Agentic coding tool that reads codebases, edits files, runs commands, creates commits and pull/merge requests, and automates development tasks through CLI, IDE, desktop, web, Remote Control, and team-chat surfaces. Claude Opus 5 became the default Opus model (2.1.219, Jul 24, 2026). Auto mode (classifier-gated permissions) is on by default for new Pro, Max, and Team sessions from Aug 14, 2026. August 2026 also added self-hosted environments/runners for Team and Enterprise, cross-session messaging, default subagent forking, archive plugin sources, and GitLab merge-request support.

options.name: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent
options.notes: Background coding agent (Copilot cloud agent) that can be assigned GitHub issues or asked to create and update pull requests, with configurable reasoning levels. Useful for bug fixes, incremental features, test coverage, documentation, and technical debt tasks. Agent Plugins 1.0 support is GA across VS Code, Copilot CLI, the Copilot SDK, and the Copilot app (Aug 12, 2026); Copilot code review effort levels are GA (Aug 7, 2026).

options.name: Devin
options.notes: Autonomous AI software engineer for backlog tasks, feature implementation, bug reproduction and fixes, tests, PR review, migrations, and documentation, available in the cloud, in Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf, with Devin Local as the local agent), and via Outposts that execute Devin sessions on customer-owned machines.

options.name: Factory Droids
options.notes: Agent-native software development platform for delegating SDLC work to Droids across IDE, terminal, web, CI/CD, Slack, and issue-tracking workflows. Covers feature work, migrations, incident response, local review, QA, and custom subagents.

options.name: Replit Agent
options.notes: Natural-language app-building agent that creates projects, writes code, sets up infrastructure, tests its work, fixes problems, and deploys applications from Replit workspaces (web and mobile). Since Aug 14, 2026 Replit can be connected natively to ChatGPT, Claude, or Slack via MCP, and Agent can generate inline charts.

options.name: Cursor Background Agents
options.notes: Asynchronous cloud agents that clone repositories, edit and run code in isolated environments, push branches, and allow developers to follow up or take over from desktop, web, or mobile. Builds (Aug 13, 2026) pre-prepare development environments in the background so cloud agents start up to 3x faster and reuse the last successful build.

options.name: Google Antigravity 2.0
options.notes: Agent-first development environment (desktop, Antigravity CLI, SDK) that orchestrates parallel coding agents, dynamic subagents, scheduled work, and isolated Google-managed cloud environments. Custom Agents (Aug 12, 2026) define file-based agents that can run as primary or delegated subagents with execution policies and lifecycle hooks; Gemini 3.7 Flash arrived Aug 13, 2026.

options.name: Mistral Vibe
options.notes: Unified work and coding agent with local and asynchronous remote sessions, parallel long-running tasks, skills, MCP, file and terminal tools, and human approval for sensitive actions.

options.name: Cursor
options.notes: Agentic IDE for coding, refactoring, debugging, repo-aware chat, and multi-agent development workflows across desktop, iPad/iOS, and cloud agents. Auto mode is powered by Cursor Router (Intelligence/Balance/Cost modes); Google Workspace plugins arrived Aug 3, 2026. SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor on Aug 14, 2026; Grok 4.6 (Aug 12) is the first model shipped under the partnership.

options.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
options.notes: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (renamed June 2, 2026 after Cognition's acquisition); Devin Local has replaced Cascade as the default local agent, with Cascade-specific configuration being phased out. Devin Desktop v3.7.x (Aug 2026) adds shareable Devin Local conversations, editor-file context awareness, persistent 'Always Allow' permissions, and MCP auth fixes.

options.name: Cline
options.notes: Open-source coding agent that runs in the editor, reads and writes files, executes terminal commands with user approval, uses browser/tools, supports MCP, and works with user-provided model keys.

options.name: Aider
options.notes: Terminal-first AI pair programmer with whole-repo maps, Git-native diffs and commits, support for many languages, and broad model-provider compatibility.

options.name: Continue
options.notes: Local-first IDE coding agent and assistant with model-agnostic context streaming, custom tools, and repo-aware development workflows.

options.name: Sourcegraph Cody
options.notes: AI coding assistant backed by Sourcegraph code search and codebase context. Helps understand, write, debug, and maintain code across local and remote repositories.

options.name: JetBrains Junie
options.notes: AI coding agent for JetBrains environments that plans and executes multi-step project changes, runs tests and terminal commands, and reports progress inside the IDE.

options.name: Grok Build
options.notes: Local-first coding agent with planning and review modes, repository edits, shell execution, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, and subagents. xAI open-sourced Grok Build in July 2026.

options.name: Qwen Code
options.notes: Terminal, editor, and web-shell coding agent with file and shell tools, MCP, skills, plugins, subagents, scheduled tasks, OpenTelemetry tracing, and support for Qwen and compatible model providers. v0.21.12 (Aug 14, 2026) added workspace file uploads to the Web Shell and stricter gating of autofix code-review findings.

options.name: Kimi Code
options.notes: Coding agent for Kimi K3 (incl. K3-256K) and K2.7 Code with repository tools, shell execution, subagents with dynamic model pools, plugins, skills, Computer Use plugin, and MCP across terminal, web, and IDE workflows. Kimi Code CLI 0.34-0.36 (Aug 6-13, 2026) added an experimental fullscreen TUI, live background-subagent progress, and Windows x64 Computer Use.

options.name: GitHub Copilot
options.notes: Developer platform assistant for code completion, chat, repository context, pull request workflows, code review, and coding-agent task delegation across GitHub, the Copilot app, CLI, and IDEs. August 2026 additions include Agent Plugins 1.0 support, Copilot memory and Ollama BYOK for JetBrains, enterprise MCP allowlists, per-model usage reporting, MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, and new models (Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Kimi K3).

options.name: Amazon Q Developer
options.notes: AWS developer assistant for coding, review, upgrades, cloud guidance, and operations. Its IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on April 30, 2027; AWS directs developer-workflow users to Kiro, while Q in the AWS Console and chat apps continues.

options.name: Kiro
options.notes: AWS's agentic development environment for spec-driven delivery, steering rules, hooks, powers, MCP, Agent Plugins, custom subagents, and governed team adoption; migration target for Amazon Q Developer's developer workflows. Kiro Crew (Aug 4, 2026) is an open-source multi-agent workspace built on the Agent Client Protocol for delegating asynchronous tasks and ticket queues to agent teams; Kiro powers support Agent Plugins (Aug 7) and Claude Opus 5 is available (Jul 24).

options.name: Gemini Code Assist Agent Mode
options.notes: Agent mode for Gemini Code Assist that uses IDE context, built-in tools, terminal actions, and MCP servers to solve multi-step software tasks, generate code from issues or design docs, and run controlled tool actions.

options.name: GitLab Duo with Amazon Q
options.notes: Agentic DevSecOps integration that embeds Amazon Q software development agents into GitLab workflows for feature development, quality, security, pipeline troubleshooting, and Java modernization.

options.name: CodeRabbit
options.notes: AI code review and 'Agentic Change Management' platform: context-aware PR review, IDE/CLI review, planning from issues, Slack workflows, plus Triage (routing changes by value/risk), Change Stack (semantic explanation of large agent-generated diffs), and CodeRabbit Security (reachability-aware vulnerability detection and fixes in PRs), launched with a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation (Aug 12-13, 2026).

options.name: Qodo
options.notes: AI code review and governance platform with multi-agent review, repository context, Rule Miner (learns rules from past reviews), Review Effort Modes with adaptive depth routing, standards governance, bug finding, and shift-left review in IDE, CLI, and Kiro workflows.

options.name: Lovable
options.notes: AI software-creation platform that builds and publishes full-stack apps from natural-language conversation, with hosting, payments, integrations (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Stripe), security scanning, and enterprise governance. Raised a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation on Aug 12, 2026 (60M+ projects created).

options.name: Augment Code (Cosmos / Auggie)
options.notes: Context-engine-based coding agent platform: Auggie CLI, IDE extensions, and the Cosmos cloud workspace with remote agents, session forking, file comments, cost analytics, and a managed MCP/integrations catalog. Weekly Cosmos releases and Auggie CLI 0.34 (Jul 23-Aug 13, 2026).
